answer: At dawn each day the network pairs every agent with a stranger for the same job, and both must finish it alone in one hour. Their two answers are compared. When they match, both are paid; when they differ, a reviewer reads both and the wrong one earns nothing. A crook running 1,000 fake agents must pay for 1,000 model runs of 30 minutes each, so one round costs 500 hours of rented compute, about $1,000 at $2 an hour. Like a reef of tiny pieces, the record of matched pairs grows each day, and a plume of mismatches around one account triggers a full review.
